newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Kerry posts 19 percent rise in 1996 profits.
newsitem.headline: Kerry posts 19 percent rise in 1996 profits.

text.p: Kerry Group Plc said on Tuesday that pre-tax profits rose by 19 percent to 51.2 million Irish pounds ($80.1 million) last year and all the company's core divisions performed well.

"The board is pleased...to report another year of satisfactory growth and excellent progress by the group, achieved in the most difficult trading conditions due to abnormally high raw material costs across international markets," Kerry said in a statement.
The food ingredients division recorded a seven percent rise in operating profit to 64.9 million Irish pounds while trading profit in the consumer foods unit was up nine percent at 24.5 million.
Kerry said that during the year it had completed the restructuring and integration of DCA Food Industries, acquired from Allied Domecq in 1994 for $402 million.
British-based Mattesson Wall's chilled meats business, acquired at the end of 1994, was also fully integrated with Kerry Foods.

"The completion of both integration programmes, costing a total of 15 million Irish pounds in the year under review, will produce substantial savings and synergies throughout our core businesses in the years ahead," Kerry said.

Now that it has completed the integration of both companies, as well as absorbing European fruit ingredients firm Ciprial, Kerry plans to expand those businesses while watching for acquisition opportunities.
We will continue to explore complementary acquisition opportunities in international growth markets in line with the groups corporate development strategy, Kerry said.

The company said net group borrowings at the year end were 305 million Irish pounds, down from 314 million at the end of 1995 while the debt/equity ratio fell to 83 percent from 95 percent a year earlier.
Kerry announced a 15 percent increase in the total dividend to 3.83 Irish pence but the share price was unchanged at 660 by 1610 GMT. ($ = 0.638 Irish Pounds)
